places.name: Băng Tâm Các
places.where: Region 7 (Ngọc Hồ Sơn), far north. On the map the place is a large island of black lava in a cold sea, about ten tiles (some 250 km) across, with smaller rocky islets off its eastern shore. Tundra, sea level at the coast. The volcano Chúc Long Sơn stands about 125 km away; it buried the old school Hồ Thiên Phái under lava in 425. Water 61 %, Ice 22. The great sect of Ice: about 150-200 cultivators and thousands of residents with servants, artisans, candidates and families; the Vessel Hall (the head's court), the Array Hall under it, the Plum Sword Hall, the Hall of Cold Law, the disciples' quarters; the Jade Vessel Array laid into the ice over the buried vent in 470.
places.imagined: A clear winter afternoon, low gold sun, seen from as high as a cloud. The island is enormous and runs off the edges of the picture, black lava frosted white, with fjords and ice cliffs along the near coast. Over the heart of the island the founder laid a sheet of blue glacier ice some ten kilometres across, as flat as a frozen lake, and on it stands a white city of ice: an outer town of hundreds of white houses, workshops and storehouses for the servants and artisans, laid out on straight frozen streets and canals; inside it a second wall; then terrace after terrace of halls rising up a black lava mountain the cultivators carved into steps, every terrace walled and gated, with long covered galleries and bridges of ice joining them. On the summit, the Vessel Hall, as big as an emperor's palace, and behind it a white pagoda thirty storeys high. Beneath the whole city, under the ice, a ring of jade-green light kilometres wide glows up through the ice, steam rising along it. At the foot of the mountain, the green-tiled roof of the old buried pagoda sticks out of a lava field the sect has kept bare as a memorial. Sledges and ice-elk trains on the frozen roads, and specks of people everywhere.
places.subject: The place: Băng Tâm Các, the great sect of Ice, a white city of halls built by cultivators on a vast black lava island in a cold northern sea. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; the island is enormous and runs off the edges of the frame, its black lava frosted white, with ice cliffs and fjords along the near coast and a dark sea scattered with drifting ice beyond; small rocky islets off the eastern shore; far away on the horizon a dark volcano sends up one thin thread of smoke. The ice: over the heart of the island lies a sheet of flat, glassy blue glacier ice about ten kilometres across. The sect, at true and grand scale, fills most of the frame: (1) an outer town on the ice of hundreds of white-walled houses, workshops, storehouses and stables with grey-blue tile roofs, laid out along straight frozen streets and canals, enclosed by a high white outer wall with great gate towers; (2) inside it a second, higher wall; (3) at the centre a black lava mountain carved by the cultivators into nine broad walled terraces, each terrace lined with large white halls, courtyards and plum gardens, joined by long covered galleries, stairways and arched bridges of clear ice; (4) on the summit the Vessel Hall, a white palace as large as an emperor's, on a white stone platform, and behind it a slender white pagoda some thirty storeys high, the tallest thing on the island. Signature elements: beneath the whole city, under the ice, a ring of glowing jade-green light kilometres wide shines up through the ice like a halo, with soft walls of steam rising along it; and at the foot of the mountain the green-tiled, curled roof-tip of an old pagoda sticks up out of a bare black lava field kept as a memorial, the only green in the white city. Life at scale: sledges and trains of pale ice-elk on the frozen roads, and thousands of tiny figures in white on the streets and terraces. Light: low golden winter sun from the upper left, long blue shadows to the lower right, a cold clear sky.
places.size: A great sect's domain about ten kilometres across on a 250 km island: an outer town of hundreds of houses and workshops, two walls, a black lava mountain carved into nine terraces, a palace-sized Vessel Hall and a thirty-storey pagoda; thousands of residents.
